```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

# API Reference

<div class="info-box">
<strong>Base URL:</strong> <code>https://api.internetofwildlife.com</code>
<br>
<strong>Protocol:</strong> HTTPS
<br>
<strong>Method:</strong> All endpoints use POST
<br>
<strong>Encoding:</strong> JSON
<br>
<strong>Timeout:</strong> 60 seconds per request
</div>

All endpoints require an API token passed in the JSON request body as `token`. The token is loaded from a `.env` file via `dotenv` and accessed with `Sys.getenv("MY_TOKEN")`.

```{r}
library(dotenv)
load_dot_env()
my_token <- Sys.getenv("MY_TOKEN")
```

## Typical Workflow

```
1. Authenticate       load_dot_env() -> Sys.getenv("MY_TOKEN")
2. List projects      POST /station/api/projects
3. List stations      POST /station/api/stations/         (per project)
4. List files         POST /station/api/file-list          (per station, paginated)
5. Download files     POST /station/api/download-file/     (per file)
6. (Optional) Import  file_handle() -> db_prep() -> db_insert()
```

The `get_my_data()` function orchestrates this entire workflow in a single call.

## POST Wrapper

All endpoints (except direct calls in `get_my_projects` and `project_list`) go through the `post()` function in `R/post.R`:

```{r}
post(endpoint, payload = NULL, show_progress = FALSE)
```

* Automatically injects `token = my_token` into every request
* 60-second timeout on all requests
* Detects HTTP 503 and emits a warning suggesting narrower date ranges or pagination
* Calls `httr::stop_for_status()` to raise on other HTTP errors
* Optional progress bar via `httr::progress()`

<hr class="section-divider">

### Parameters

<table class="param-table">
<thead>
<tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Description</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
  <td><code>token</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">string</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-required">REQUIRED</span></td>
  <td>API authentication token</td>
</tr>
<tr>

### curl Example

```{bash}
curl -X POST https://api.internetofwildlife.com/station/api/stations/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"token": "YOUR_API_TOKEN", "project-id": "YOUR_PROJECT_ID"}'
```

### Response

<div class="response-section">

**200 OK**

```json
{
  "stations": [
    {
      "station": {
        "id": "STATION-001"
      },
```

## List Station Files <span class="tag-label tag-files">Files</span>

<div class="endpoint-header">
<span class="method-badge method-post">POST</span>
<span class="endpoint-path">/station/api/file-list</span>
</div>

Retrieves metadata for data files available from a specific station, with optional date range and file type filtering. Supports pagination via `limit` and `offset`.

### Parameters

<table class="param-table">
<thead>
<tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Description</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
  <td><code>token</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">string</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-required">REQUIRED</span></td>
  <td>API authentication token</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>station-id</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">string</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-required">REQUIRED</span></td>
  <td>Station identifier obtained from the List Stations endpoint</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>begin</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">date</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-required">REQUIRED</span></td>
  <td>Start date for file search (ISO date format, e.g. <code>2024-01-01</code>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>end</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">date</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-optional">optional</span></td>
  <td>End date for file search. Defaults to today if omitted.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>file-types</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">string[]</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-optional">optional</span></td>
  <td>Filter by file types: <code>data</code>, <code>node-data</code>, <code>gps</code>, <code>log</code>, <code>telemetry</code>, <code>sensorgnome</code>, <code>ble</code>, <code>blu</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>limit</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">integer</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-optional">optional</span></td>
  <td>Maximum number of files to return (for pagination)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>offset</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">integer</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-optional">optional</span></td>
  <td>Number of files to skip (for pagination)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### curl Examples

**Basic request (required fields only):**

```{bash}
curl -X POST https://api.internetofwildlife.com/station/api/file-list \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"token": "YOUR_API_TOKEN", "station-id": "YOUR_STATION_ID", "begin": "2024-01-01"}'
```

**Full request with all options:**

```{bash}
curl -X POST https://api.internetofwildlife.com/station/api/file-list \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "token": "YOUR_API_TOKEN",
    "station-id": "YOUR_STATION_ID",
    "begin": "2024-01-01",
    "end": "2024-02-01",
    "file-types": ["data", "gps"],
    "limit": 100,
    "offset": 0
  }'
```

### Response

<div class="response-section">

**200 OK**

```json
{
  "files": [
    {
      "id": "file-789",
      "name": "CTT-STATION001-data.csv.gz"
    },
    {
      "id": "file-790",
      "name": "CTT-STATION001-gps.csv.gz"
    }
  ]
}
```

</div>

<div class="info-box">
<strong>Note:</strong> Large date ranges may cause 503 server timeouts. Use <code>get_station_file_list_paginated()</code> to handle this automatically. The paginated version retries failed chunks up to <code>max_retries</code> times (default 3) with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 6s).
</div>

### Errors

<table class="error-table">
<thead>
<tr><th>Status</th><th>Cause</th><th>What You See</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">401</span></td>
  <td>Invalid or expired API token</td>
  <td><code>httr::stop_for_status()</code> raises: <code>"Unauthorized (HTTP 401)"</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">503</span></td>
  <td>Date range too large; server times out</td>
  <td>Warning: <code>"Server query timeout — try narrowing your date range or using pagination"</code>. The paginated wrapper catches this and retries: <code>"Request timed out, retrying (attempt X of Y)..."</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">Timeout</span></td>
  <td>Network issue or server unreachable</td>
  <td>R error: <code>"Timeout was reached"</code> after 60 seconds. Paginated wrapper retries up to <code>max_retries</code> times with exponential backoff.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">Invalid type</span></td>
  <td>A value in <code>file-types</code> is not one of the 8 valid types</td>
  <td>Warning: <code>"WARNING: invalid file type specified - ignoring: &lt;type&gt;"</code>. Invalid types are dropped; request proceeds with valid types only.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">404</span></td>
  <td><code>station-id</code> does not exist</td>
  <td><code>httr::stop_for_status()</code> stops execution with an HTTP error</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">Empty result</span></td>
  <td>Station has no files for the given date range</td>
  <td><code>get_data()</code> prints <code>"no files found from API"</code> and returns an empty list</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">Max retries</span></td>
  <td>Paginated wrapper exhausts all retry attempts on a chunk</td>
  <td>The original error is re-thrown via <code>stop(e)</code>, halting execution</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### R Package Functions

<div class="used-by">

<span class="method-badge method-post">POST</span>
<span class="endpoint-path">/station/api/download-file/</span>
</div>

Downloads the contents of a single data file by its ID.

### Parameters

<table class="param-table">
<thead>
<tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Description</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>bypass-encoding</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">string</span></td>

  <td>Set to <code>"plain"</code> to bypass encoding. Used automatically as a fallback on retry.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### curl Examples

**Basic download:**

```{bash}
curl -X POST https://api.internetofwildlife.com/station/api/download-file/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"token": "YOUR_API_TOKEN", "file-id": "YOUR_FILE_ID"}'
```

**With bypass encoding (fallback on error):**

```{bash}
curl -X POST https://api.internetofwildlife.com/station/api/download-file/ \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"token": "YOUR_API_TOKEN", "file-id": "YOUR_FILE_ID", "bypass-encoding": "plain"}'
```

### Response

<div class="response-section">

**200 OK** — Raw file content (CSV text, UTF-8 encoded)

```
TagId,NodeId,TagRSSI,Validated,Time
TAG-001,NODE-A,-70,1,2024-01-15 12:00:00
TAG-001,NODE-B,-85,1,2024-01-15 12:00:00
```

In batch downloads via `get_data()`, each file result is tracked in a dataframe. The final summary prints: `"Download complete: X succeeded, Y failed out of Z files"`

</div>

### Errors

<table class="error-table">
<thead>
<tr><th>Status</th><th>Cause</th><th>What You See</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">401</span></td>
  <td>Invalid or expired API token</td>
  <td><code>httr::stop_for_status()</code> raises: <code>"Unauthorized (HTTP 401)"</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">404</span></td>
  <td><code>file-id</code> does not match any file on the server</td>
  <td><code>httr::stop_for_status()</code> stops execution with an HTTP error</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">500</span></td>
  <td>File content has encoding issues the server can't handle</td>
  <td><code>download_files()</code> prints <code>"Here's the original error message:"</code> followed by the error detail, then automatically retries with <code>bypass-encoding = "plain"</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">500 (retry)</span></td>
  <td>File is corrupted or unrecoverable (retry also fails)</td>
  <td>Error propagates up; <code>get_data()</code> catches it per-file and records <code>status = "failed"</code> in results dataframe</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">503</span></td>
  <td>Server overloaded or temporarily down</td>
  <td>Warning: <code>"Server query timeout — try narrowing your date range or using pagination"</code>, then execution stops</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">Timeout</span></td>
  <td>Network issue or server unreachable</td>
  <td>R error: <code>"Timeout was reached"</code> after 60 seconds</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">Batch failure</span></td>
  <td>Any error during a single file download within <code>get_data()</code></td>
  <td>File is marked <code>"failed"</code> in the results dataframe; remaining files continue. Final summary: <code>"Download complete: X succeeded, Y failed out of Z files"</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## Station Checkins <span class="tag-label tag-checkins">Checkins</span>

<div class="endpoint-header">
<span class="method-badge method-get">GET</span>
<span class="endpoint-path">/station/station-data/{station_id}/</span>
</div>

Retrieves the checkin history for a single sensor station. Stations check in periodically, reporting GPS position, modem signal, disk and memory usage, uptime, and the number of beeps and unique tags heard since the last checkin.

<div class="info-box">
<strong>Different host and authentication:</strong> this endpoint is served by <code>https://account.celltracktech.com</code>, not <code>api.internetofwildlife.com</code>. It does <strong>not</strong> accept the API token. It uses a logged-in session cookie, so you sign in with your CTT account username and password first (see the curl example below).
<br>
<strong>Method:</strong> GET
<br>
<strong>Limit:</strong> returns at most the 500 most recent checkins, newest first, starting from the station's current deployment date
</div>

### Parameters

<table class="param-table">
<thead>
<tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Description</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
  <td><code>station_id</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">string</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-required">REQUIRED</span></td>
  <td>Station identifier, passed in the URL path (e.g. <code>V30B0001</code>). The same ID returned as <code>station.id</code> by the List Stations endpoint.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>sessionid</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">cookie</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-required">REQUIRED</span></td>
  <td>Session cookie set by logging in at <code>/accounts/login/</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### curl Example

Logging in takes two requests: one to fetch the login form's CSRF token and one to submit your credentials. The cookies are saved to a cookie jar file and reused for the checkin request.

```{bash}
BASE=https://account.celltracktech.com
JAR=/tmp/ctt-cookies.txt
USERNAME=YOUR_CTT_USERNAME
STATION=YOUR_STATION_ID
read -s -p "Password: " PASSWORD; echo

# 1. Fetch the login page (sets the csrftoken cookie) and extract the form token
TOKEN=$(curl -c "$JAR" "$BASE/accounts/login/" \
  | grep csrfmiddlewaretoken | head -1 \
  | sed -E "s/.*value=['\"]([^'\"]+)['\"].*/\1/")

# 2. Log in (expect HTTP 302)
curl -b "$JAR" -c "$JAR" -e "$BASE/accounts/login/" \
  -X POST "$BASE/accounts/login/" \
  --data-urlencode "csrfmiddlewaretoken=$TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "username=$USERNAME" \
  --data-urlencode "password=$PASSWORD" \
  -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n"
unset PASSWORD

# 3. Get the station's checkins
curl -b "$JAR" "$BASE/station/station-data/$STATION/"
```

**Only the most recent checkin** (requires <code>jq</code>):

```{bash}
curl -b "$JAR" "$BASE/station/station-data/$STATION/" | jq '.checkins[0]'
```

### Response

<div class="response-section">

**200 OK**

```json
{
  "checkins": [
    {
      "station": {
        "id": "V30B0001",
        "imei": "359073061234567",
        "sim": "8901260000000000000",
        "created_at": "2024-01-10T15:22:01.000000+00:00"
      },
      "project": "My Wildlife Project",
      "alias": "North Field",
      "received_at": "2024-05-18T12:00:04.512000+00:00",
      "lat": 40.0,
      "lng": -75.0,
      "bootcount": 3,
      "uptime": 12345,
      "cpu": 8,
      "free_memory": 900000,
      "available_space": 25000000,
      "beeps_since_last_checkin": 19,
      "unique_tags_since_last_checkin": 2,
      "pending_uploads": null,
      "software_update": "2.1.0",
      "software": null,
      "image": "2.0.5",
      "modem": {
        "signal": -71,
        "carrier": "VZW",
        "updated_at": "2024-05-18T12:00:00+00:00"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Key fields in each checkin:

* **`received_at`**: ISO 8601 timestamp when the server received the checkin
* **`lat`** / **`lng`**: GPS position (null if the station had no GPS fix)
* **`beeps_since_last_checkin`**: total tag detections since the previous checkin
* **`unique_tags_since_last_checkin`**: number of distinct tags heard since the previous checkin
* **`cpu`**: 15-minute load average
* **`modem.signal`**: cellular signal strength (dBm)

</div>

### Errors

<table class="error-table">
<thead>
<tr><th>Status</th><th>Cause</th><th>What You See</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">302 / HTML</span></td>
  <td>Not logged in, or the session cookie has expired</td>
  <td>The response is the HTML login page instead of JSON. Repeat steps 1–2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">403</span></td>
  <td>Login POST sent without a valid CSRF token or <code>Referer</code> header</td>
  <td>Django "CSRF verification failed" page. Make sure step 1 ran and <code>-e</code> is set in step 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">404</span></td>
  <td><code>station_id</code> does not exist, the station has no deployment, or your account is not a member of the station's project</td>
  <td>HTML "Not Found" page</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">Empty list</span></td>
  <td>Station has not checked in since its current deployment began</td>
  <td>Response returns <code>"checkins": []</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### R Package Functions

<div class="used-by">

* None yet. This endpoint is not wrapped by the <code>celltracktech</code> R package; call it with curl or <code>httr</code> directly.

</div>

<hr class="section-divider">

## Station Data Files <span class="tag-label tag-files">Files</span>

The **Data Files** tabs on a station's page in the sensor station portal (<code>https://account.celltracktech.com/station/station-home/{station_id}/</code>) list every file the station has uploaded since its current deployment, with a download link for each one. The two endpoints below give you the same lists and downloads from the command line. Like Station Checkins, they need a logged-in session cookie, not the API token.

### File Types

Each portal tab corresponds to one file type. Replace <code>{station_id}</code> with your station's ID and <code>{file_id}</code> with an <code>id</code> from the file list.

<table class="param-table">
<thead>
<tr><th>Portal Tab</th><th>File Type</th><th>Contents</th><th>File List</th><th>Download</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
  <td>Radio</td>
  <td><code>data</code></td>
  <td>Tag detections (beeps) from the station's radios</td>
  <td><code>POST /station/files/data/{station_id}/</code></td>
  <td rowspan="7"><code>GET /station/download-file/{file_id}/</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td>Node Health</td>
  <td><code>node-data</code></td>
  <td>Health reports from nodes (battery, solar, RSSI)</td>
  <td><code>POST /station/files/node-data/{station_id}/</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td>Log</td>
  <td><code>log</code></td>
  <td>Station software log</td>
  <td><code>POST /station/files/log/{station_id}/</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td>GPS</td>
  <td><code>gps</code></td>
  <td>Station GPS position fixes</td>
  <td><code>POST /station/files/gps/{station_id}/</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td>Telemetry</td>
  <td><code>telemetry</code></td>
  <td>Station telemetry data</td>
  <td><code>POST /station/files/telemetry/{station_id}/</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td>BlūSeries</td>
  <td><code>ble</code></td>
  <td>BlūSeries tag detections. Uploads named <code>blu</code> or <code>ble</code> are both stored under this type.</td>
  <td><code>POST /station/files/ble/{station_id}/</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td>Sensorgnome</td>
  <td><code>sensorgnome</code></td>
  <td>Sensorgnome-format detections, shared with <a href="https://motus.org">Motus</a></td>
  <td><code>POST /station/files/sensorgnome/{station_id}/</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<div class="info-box">
<strong>Note:</strong> the portal only lists files from the station's <strong>current</strong> deployment. To get files from earlier deployments or a specific date range, use the token-based <a href="#list-station-files-files">List Station Files</a> endpoint.
</div>

### List Files

<div class="endpoint-header">
<span class="method-badge method-post">POST</span>
<span class="endpoint-path">/station/files/{file_type}/{station_id}/</span>
</div>

Returns one page of files of the given type, newest first. This is the request the portal makes when you open a tab.

<table class="param-table">
<thead>
<tr><th>Field</th><th>Type</th><th>Required</th><th>Description</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
  <td><code>file_type</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">string</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-required">REQUIRED</span></td>
  <td>One of the file types in the table above, in the URL path</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>station_id</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">string</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-required">REQUIRED</span></td>
  <td>Station identifier, in the URL path</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>start</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">integer</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-required">REQUIRED</span></td>
  <td>Number of files to skip (form field)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>length</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">integer</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-required">REQUIRED</span></td>
  <td>Number of files to return (form field)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>draw</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">integer</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-required">REQUIRED</span></td>
  <td>Any integer; echoed back in the response (form field)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><code>X-CSRFToken</code></td>
  <td><span class="param-type">header</span></td>
  <td><span class="param-required">REQUIRED</span></td>
  <td>Value of the <code>csrftoken</code> cookie set at login</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

After logging in as shown in [Station Checkins](#station-checkins-checkins) (steps 1 and 2):

```{bash}
FILETYPE=data
CSRF=$(awk '$6=="csrftoken"{print $7}' "$JAR")

curl -b "$JAR" -e "$BASE/station/station-home/$STATION/" \
  -H "X-CSRFToken: $CSRF" \
  -X POST "$BASE/station/files/$FILETYPE/$STATION/" \
  --data-urlencode 'draw=1' \
  --data-urlencode 'start=0' \
  --data-urlencode 'length=10'
```

<div class="response-section">

**200 OK**

```json
{
  "draw": 1,
  "recordsTotal": 412,
  "recordsFiltered": 412,
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 18234567,
      "file_at": "2024-05-18T12:00:00+00:00",
      "filetype": "data",
      "filename": "CTT-V30B0001-raw-data.2024-05-18_120000.csv.gz",
      "bytes": 48213
    }
  ]
}
```

<code>recordsTotal</code> is the total number of files of this type. Increase <code>start</code> by <code>length</code> to page through them.

</div>

### Download a File

<div class="endpoint-header">
<span class="method-badge method-get">GET</span>
<span class="endpoint-path">/station/download-file/{file_id}/</span>
</div>

Downloads one file using the <code>id</code> from the file list. This is the portal's **Download** button. The file is gzip-compressed CSV, so save it with a <code>.csv.gz</code> extension or pipe it through <code>gunzip</code>.

```{bash}
FILE_ID=18234567

# Save the compressed file
curl -b "$JAR" "$BASE/station/download-file/$FILE_ID/" -o "$FILE_ID.csv.gz"

# Or decompress on the fly
curl -b "$JAR" "$BASE/station/download-file/$FILE_ID/" | gunzip > "$FILE_ID.csv"
```

### Errors

<table class="error-table">
<thead>
<tr><th>Status</th><th>Cause</th><th>What You See</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">302 / HTML</span></td>
  <td>Not logged in, or the session cookie has expired</td>
  <td>The HTML login page instead of JSON or file contents</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">403</span></td>
  <td>File list request sent without the <code>X-CSRFToken</code> header or <code>Referer</code></td>
  <td>Django "CSRF verification failed" page</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">404</span></td>
  <td>Unknown file type or station, your account is not on the station's project, or the file is from an earlier deployment</td>
  <td>HTML "Not Found" page</td>
</tr>
<tr>
  <td><span class="error-code">500</span></td>
  <td><code>draw</code>, <code>start</code> or <code>length</code> missing from the file list request</td>
  <td>HTML "Server Error" page</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

### R Package Functions

<div class="used-by">

* None. To download files with the R package, use <code>get_my_data()</code>, which uses the token-based [List Station Files](#list-station-files-files) and [Download File](#download-file-files) endpoints.

</div>
